name: Larry Page
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Larry Page stepped down as CEO of Alphabet, the parent company of Google, in 2019 but remains a board member and a controlling shareholder.
He cofounded Google in 1998 with fellow Stanford Ph.D. student Sergey Brin.
With Brin, Page invented Google's PageRank algorithm, which powers the search engine.
Page was CEO until 2001, when Eric Schmidt took over, and then from 2011 until 2015, when he became CEO of Google's new parent firm Alphabet.
forbes_facts: Page has avoided public appearances since Sundar Pichai became Google's CEO, including Alphabet's 2019 shareholders meeting -- much to investors' chagrin.
Page is a clean energy advocate; his Palo Alto home uses fuel cells and geothermal energy.

name: Emmanuel Besnier
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Emmanuel Besnier is the controlling shareholder of family-held Lactalis, the world's largest dairy conglomerate, with more than $30 billion in annual revenues.
His grandfather founded the company in 1933. It now sells products including President brie, Siggi's yogurt and Stonyfield.
His younger siblings, Jean-Michel and Marie, split the rest of the ownership in the family's milk and cheese giant.
The world's biggest dairy company, Lactalis now employs 85,000 and owns more than 266 plants in 51 countries.
forbes_facts: Besnier has been called the "French Howard Hughes,"  "the Emperor of Cheese," and, thanks to his disdain for the press, "the invisible billionaire."
On his first day in business, Besnier's father collected 17 liters of milk and made 35 camemberts.

name: Kwong Siu-hing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2021-2025); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Kwong Siu-hing is the widow of Sun Hung Kai Properties cofounder Kwok Tak-seng, who died in 1990.
She served as the company's chairman from 2008 to 2011 after her eldest son, Walter, was ousted in a feud with her two other sons Thomas and Raymond.
She remains the biggest shareholder in Sun Hung Kai.
Raymond has been the sole chairman since Thomas was sentenced to five years in prison in 2014 for bribery; he was released in 2019. Walter died in 2018.
forbes_facts: Kwong left Guangdong Province in mainland China for Hong Kong in 1947 and married Kwok at the age of 20.
Kwok started the company with Fung King-hey and Lee Shau Kee in 1958. It went public in 1972 and has become one of Hong Kong's largest developers.

name: Mike Brown
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Mike Brown and his family own the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals, which Forbes valued at more than $5 billion in 2025.
He helped his father, Paul, found the team in 1967 after the elder Brown was fired as the Cleveland Browns coach in 1963.
Several members of the Brown family are involved with the team today, including Mike's daughter Katie, who was the first woman to be named to the NFL's Competition Committee.

name: Rakesh Gangwal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Airline veteran Rakesh Gangwal owes his fortune to InterGlobe Aviation, the parent outfit of budget airline IndiGo, India's largest by market share.
Gangwal started his airline career with United Airlines in 1984 and went on to run US Airways Group as its chief executive and chairman.
Gangwal cofounded IndiGo, headquartered outside Delhi, with Rahul Bhatia (also a billionaire) in 2006 with one aircraft.
The Miami resident resigned from the company's board in 2022 and said he would gradually sell his stock over the next five years.
Gangwal was named chairman of Southwest Airlines in November 2024. He resigned from that role in August 2025 but remains on the board.
forbes_facts: The Indian-born mechanical engineer studied at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur before getting his M.B.A. at Wharton.
He and his wife paid $30 million for a Miami mansion that previously belonged to billionaire Charles Johnson.
Gangwal and IndiGo cofounder Bhatia had a bitter falling out in 2019 over corporate governance issues. Their dispute reached courts in London, Florida and Maryland.

name: Vladimir Kim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Vladimir Kim joined Kazakhstan mineral firm Kazakhmys in 1995 after earning degrees in civil engineering, economics and business administration.
He was named chairman in 2005, before Kazakhmys became the first Kazakh company to list on the London Stock Exchange.
In a 2014 restructuring, Kazakhmys de-merged into private company Kazakhmys Corp. and a separate public company, KAZ Minerals plc.
Kim still has a stake in KAZ Minerals and sold his majority stake in Kazakhmys Corp., which inherited most of the group's mature mining (mostly copper) assets, in 2025.
He stepped down as chairman of KAZ Minerals in 2013.
forbes_facts: He is a descendent of Koreans forced by Stalin to move to Kazakhstan.

name: Zhenhua Yao
forbes_bio: Yao Zhenhua was barely known before an insurer he controls started to buy shares in property developer China Vanke, where he holds a 25% stake.
Regulators unhappy with trading by Yao's insurer Foresea Life in 2017 barred him from holding a position in the industry for a decade.
Yao founded Baoneng Group in 1992 as a retailing business; today it has more than 40 shopping malls around China and is involved in healthcare.

name: Cai Huabo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Cai Lijiang is the chairman of Shenzhen Longsys Electronics, a supplier of memory and storage products.
Cai became a billionaire following the company's IPO on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2022.
Longsys acquired the Lexar brand from U.S. chipmaker Micron in 2017.

name: April Goh
forbes_bio: April Goh is a granddaughter of the late Singaporean paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang, who died in August 2025 at age 98.
The Goh family draws the bulk of its wealth from a majority stake in Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings, one of the world's largest paint manufacturers.
April, together with her five cousins, inherited the bulk of their grandfather's fortune.
Her father is Cheun Jin, the younger son of the late patriarch who started making paints in a small factory in Singapore before partnering with Nippon Paint in 1962.
She is currently a graduate student at Columbia University School of Social Work.

name: Laurence Graff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Graff Diamonds International chairman Laurence Graff operates at the top of the diamond jewelry market, with more than 60 retail stores worldwide.
Graff clients have included Donald Trump, Oprah Winfrey, Larry Ellison, Elizabeth Taylor and the Sultan of Brunei.
He built his business from nothing, after dropping out of school at 14 and scrubbing toilets as a jeweler's apprentice in London's Hatton Garden.
He owns a polished diamond trading firm in Switzerland, real estate in London's Mayfair district and a stake in a S. African diamond wholesaler.
He also owns Delaire Graff Estate, a vineyard and winery with a boutique hotel and restaurant in Stellenbosch, the Napa Valley of South Africa.
forbes_facts: Graff splits his time between homes in Gstaad, London, St. Tropez, New York City and his 150-foot Feadship yacht.
Graff's modern and contemporary art collection is worth more than $600 million and he collects vintage cars, including Ferraris, Aston Martins and Mercedes.
